size_explanation: The container has a strictly fixed size. It will be completely filled with cryptographic random bytes, making it indistinguishable from random noise.
decoy_explanation: This volume contains harmless data. If forced to provide a password, you reveal this password. The observer cannot mathematically prove anything else exists.
hidden_explanation: The hidden volume is placed at a non-deterministic position inside the random fill space. Its existence is impossible to detect without the hidden password.
password_hint: Enter your password to unlock the volume.
files_extracted: Files successfully unpacked to output folder.
warning_no_modify_decoy: Never write to the decoy volume with third-party tools after creating the hidden volume, as it could overwrite the hidden data.
warning_cloud_sync: Avoid automatic cloud syncing/versioning tools (e.g. Dropbox, Google Drive), as file history might reveal prior container sizes or modification offsets.
warning_password_entropy: Use high-entropy passwords. Argon2id protects against brute force, but short passwords remain vulnerable to dictionary attacks.
kdf_warning_floor: Warning: Parameters below 64 MB / 2 iterations are not recommended for production security.
about_text: QuietBox is an open-source plausible deniability volume cryptor designed for activists, journalists, and individuals in coercive environments. Built with Rust, Tauri, and SvelteKit.
drop_files_here: Drag and drop files or folders here
or_click_to_browse: or click to select from disk
